term.value: Shopping Center Lease 1/29/1998; possession 11/6/1998; Commencement 2/4/1999. Initial Term of 15 years, then FIVE 5-year renewal options (Article 5) that AUTO-EXERCISE unless Tenant gives ≥120 days' notice NOT to renew. PetSmart has let options 1–3 run (the 2024 notice confirms the third option commencing 2/1/2025), so the current term runs to 1/31/2030, with two options remaining (to 1/31/2040).

cite.doc: Lease Art. 5; First Amendment; Renewal Notice

options.note: CURRENT period (Lease Years 26–30); auto-exercised, confirmed by the 8/19/2024 courtesy notice.
Lease Years 36–40 — final option, fully optioned expiry 1/31/2040.

optionNotes: Five 5-year renewal options total (Article 5), auto-exercising unless Tenant gives ≥120 days' notice NOT to renew. Full base-rent ladder (First Amendment, certified to 15,250 SF — stated as 'Maximum' base rent, which the rent roll confirms is the actual): Initial Term — Yrs 1–5 $19.26/SF ($293,715), Yrs 6–10 $20.76 ($316,590), Yrs 11–15 $22.26 ($339,465); Renewals — Yrs 16–20 $23.50 ($358,375), Yrs 21–25 $25.00 ($381,250), Yrs 26–30 $26.50 ($404,125, current), Yrs 31–35 $28.00 ($427,000), Yrs 36–40 $29.50 ($449,875). $1.50/SF step per renewal.

percentageRent.value: None. Base Rent only (with CPI / floor-area / hard-building-cost adjustments that were fixed by the First Amendment). No percentage/overage rent.

exclusives.description: PET-STORE exclusive (Exhibit I §2): PetSmart's 'Primary Business' = retail sale of (i) pets, (ii) pet/animal food, accessories and products (incl. equestrian), (iii) pet/animal services (grooming, boarding, veterinary), (iv) nature/environment products, and (v) related educational products. Excluding King Soopers, OfficeMax and Home Place (and successors), no other Center tenant may engage in clauses (i)–(iii) of the Primary Business except on an incidental basis. Survives 6 months post-term (unless Tenant leaves the metro or the lease is terminated for Tenant default).

coTenancy.value: EXPIRED / not currently operative. Exhibit K provided a King Soopers protection ONLY during the first 5 years after Commencement (2/4/1999–2/4/2004): if King Soopers went dark 12 months, Base Rent would drop 25% until King Soopers or a Comparable Replacement Tenant reopened (or the 5-year window ended). The Initial Co-Tenants were King Soopers, OfficeMax and Home Place. There is NO ongoing co-tenancy protection today.

camTax.value: CAM (Lease Art. 11.6): Tenant pays its Proportionate Share of Common Area Costs + a 5% administrative fee. Excludes capital costs, structural repairs, management/leasing/marketing, depreciation and financing. Estimated CAM (excl. utilities/snow) capped at prior-year actual +5%. 2-year reconciliation waiver; full audit rights (3% overstatement → Landlord pays audit). NOTE: the 2011 DDR Uniform CAM Agreement had fixed CAM at $1.02/SF (2010) +2.75%/yr, but per its §5 University Hills dropped out of that agreement when KPR bought the center (2024) — so PetSmart now pays the lease's pro-rata CAM + 5% admin. Real Estate Taxes: pro-rata Proportionate Share (Art. 12).

leaseNotes.label: Security Deposit
leaseNotes.value: None

leaseNotes.label: Use Clause
leaseNotes.value: PetSmart's Primary Business (pet store with grooming/boarding/veterinary, pet products, nature/educational) or any lawful retail use typical of a comparable shopping center (subject to Exhibit I prohibited uses and other tenants' exclusives). Must open fully stocked/staffed within 18 months of Commencement; thereafter NO obligation to operate or keep any hours (subject to the go-dark recapture below).

leaseNotes.label: Radius
leaseNotes.value: None

leaseNotes.label: LL Radius
leaseNotes.value: None

leaseNotes.label: Exclusive Use
leaseNotes.value: Pet-store exclusive (Exhibit I §2): pets, pet food/accessories/products, and pet services (grooming/boarding/vet) — no other tenant may conduct these except incidentally; excludes King Soopers, OfficeMax, Home Place. Survives 6 months post-term.

leaseNotes.label: Co-tenancy
leaseNotes.value: EXPIRED. Only a first-5-years King Soopers protection (25% rent reduction on a 12-month King Soopers dark) existed (Exhibit K); that window closed 2/2004. No ongoing co-tenancy today. (PetSmart is itself one of Michaels' required co-tenancy anchors and is operating.)

leaseNotes.label: Kickout/Termination (LL)
leaseNotes.value: Landlord go-dark recapture: if Tenant ceases business for 180+ consecutive days (max twice in the Initial Term or once in any 5-year period), Landlord may terminate on 30 days' notice — but must pay Tenant a termination fee (see Go Dark). Plus casualty/condemnation rights.

leaseNotes.label: Kickout/Termination (Tenant)
leaseNotes.value: Tenant may terminate for an uncured exclusive/use violation (Termination Default) after two 30-day notices (§25.2); plus casualty/condemnation. No general early-termination right.

leaseNotes.label: LL Restrictions
leaseNotes.value: Center-wide prohibited uses (Exhibit I §1): nuisance, loud/odor uses, manufacturing, dry cleaner (ex. drop-off), used-clothing/thrift/liquidation, massage parlor, adult, mortuary, coin laundry, bar/tavern (ex. restaurant/liquor store), nightclub, cinema/theater, recreation (bowling/skating/arcade/health spa), church. Within 125 ft of the Premises (Tenant approval): drive-throughs, kids' rec/daycare, restaurants >3,500 SF, offices, professional uses, schools. Also bound by the Denver Urban Renewal use restrictions and the 7/17/1996 recorded Declaration of Restrictions.

leaseNotes.label: Tenant Restrictions
leaseNotes.value: Tenant must respect other occupants' exclusive rights (for tenants/occupants of >10,000 SF, where the exclusive is their principal business, isn't part of PetSmart's Primary Business, and Landlord has notified Tenant) and the Exhibit I prohibited uses / recorded restrictions.

leaseNotes.label: CAM Method
leaseNotes.value: Pro-rata Proportionate Share of Common Area Costs + 5% admin fee (Art. 11.6). Excludes capital, structural, management/leasing/marketing, depreciation, financing. Estimate capped at prior-year actual +5% (excl. utilities/snow). 2-year reconciliation waiver; full audit (3% overstatement → LL pays). Currently on the lease method (the 2011 DDR fixed-CAM ended when KPR bought the center).

leaseNotes.label: Tax Method
leaseNotes.value: Pro-rata Proportionate Share of Real Property Taxes (Art. 12).

leaseNotes.label: Insurance Method
leaseNotes.value: Tenant pays its Proportionate Share of Insurance Costs (separate from CAM and taxes).

leaseNotes.label: Assignment & Sublet
leaseNotes.value: Landlord consent required, not to be unreasonably withheld/conditioned/delayed (deemed granted if Landlord doesn't disapprove with reasons within 30 days); permitted retail use only (no Exhibit I/Art. 6 violation). NO consent needed for collateral assignment, a merger/consolidation/sale of substantially all of Tenant's metro-area stores, or concessions/licenses. Tenant remains liable for rent/CAM/tax/insurance.

leaseNotes.label: Alterations
leaseNotes.value: Tenant may make non-structural/interior alterations; structural/exterior changes per the lease's construction/signage provisions. Trade fixtures remain Tenant's and removable.

leaseNotes.label: Operating Covenant
leaseNotes.value: None after the initial 18-month opening covenant — no continuous-operation requirement (subject to the go-dark recapture).

leaseNotes.label: Go Dark Option
leaseNotes.value: Tenant may go dark, BUT if it ceases business for 180+ consecutive days (limited to twice in the Initial Term or once per any 5-year period), Landlord may terminate on 30 days' notice. Tenant can defeat termination by giving notice it will resume (directly or via assignee/subtenant) within 120 days and doing so. On any such Landlord termination, Landlord must pay Tenant a termination fee = greater of FMV or book value of Tenant's leasehold improvements/fixtures, capped at $500,000 (amortized straight-line over the 15-year initial term).

leaseNotes.label: Default
leaseNotes.value: Tenant default (Art. 24): 10 days to cure money defaults after notice; 30 days for non-monetary (longer if not curable in 30 and Tenant diligently pursues). Landlord must obtain a court order to re-enter/dispossess and must mitigate; standard deficiency/relet damages. No cross-defaults with other PetSmart/Landlord leases (§24.3). Landlord default (Art. 25): 30-day cure; Tenant remedies incl. termination for exclusive/use violations after two 30-day notices, self-help/offset, and a first-5-years sales-based rent-abatement formula.

leaseNotes.label: Guaranty
leaseNotes.value: None on the tenant side. (The folder's 1998 'Guarantee' is a landlord/principal COMPLETION guaranty from Gold UH/Mark Goldberg to the lender New York Life — not a guaranty of PetSmart's lease.)

leaseNotes.label: Outparcel Restrictions
leaseNotes.value: Center has pad/outparcel buildings (Buildings L/M/N/O/P) with height carve-outs; height of other in-line improvements limited to Tenant's building height except King Soopers, OfficeMax, Home Place, Hallmark and Ulta.

leaseNotes.label: Purchase Option / ROFR
leaseNotes.value: None — no purchase option or right of first refusal in the lease.

leaseNotes.label: Holdover
leaseNotes.value: Holdover handled under the lease's general provisions (specific premium not separately extracted here).

leaseNotes.label: Relocation
leaseNotes.value: None — no landlord relocation right; Tenant Control Area / parking fixed on Exhibit A.

leaseNotes.label: Utilities
leaseNotes.value: Separately metered; Tenant pays utilities serving the Premises directly.

leaseNotes.label: HVAC / Maintenance
leaseNotes.value: Tenant maintains its building/HVAC; Landlord maintains the Common Areas (structural repairs and capital are excluded from CAM and are Landlord's cost).

leaseNotes.label: Pylon / Signage
leaseNotes.value: Building signage ≥150 SF (front/back) plus secondary grooming/vet signage. Monument signs on Colorado Blvd and East Yale Ave — Tenant has a first right to an available panel (after the Retail 'J' tenant), behind King Soopers/OfficeMax/Home Place and any larger tenant. Landlord lights/maintains the monuments.

leaseNotes.label: Subordination / SNDA
leaseNotes.value: Non-disturbance protected: Landlord delivered an ALTA leasehold title policy ($1M, Stewart Title) and the lease contemplates mortgagee non-disturbance; Tenant must give a mortgagee a 30-day cure window before terminating for Landlord default. On a sale of the Center, the buyer must assume the lease for Landlord to be released (§21.4).

leaseNotes.label: Estoppel
leaseNotes.value: Customary estoppel/SNDA cooperation per the lease's general provisions.

flags.detail: The 2011 DDR Uniform CAM Agreement fixed PetSmart's CAM at $1.02/SF (2010) escalating 2.75%/yr, but §5 removes a premises from that agreement when DDR/SITE sells the center. KPR acquired University Hills in 2024, which should have dropped PetSmart out of the fixed-CAM deal and reverted it to the lease's pro-rata CAM + 5% admin. Worth confirming which basis PetSmart is actually being billed on now (the rent roll shows ~$1.575/SF monthly CAM), since it affects recoveries. Not a lease error — a billing/transition item for KPR to verify.

narrative: PetSmart (PetSmart LLC, f/k/a PetSmart, Inc.; store #0231) occupies 15,250 SF (Suite 56) at University Hills, Denver under a 1/29/1998 lease that commenced 2/4/1999. The structure is a 15-year initial term plus five 5-year options that auto-renew unless PetSmart affirmatively declines (120 days' notice); PetSmart is now in its third option (commenced 2/1/2025) at $26.50/SF ($404,125/yr), with two options remaining at $28.00 and $29.50/SF (to 1/31/2040). Rent steps $1.50/SF per renewal; there is no percentage rent and no tenant guaranty. The lease carries a pet-store exclusive (pets, pet products, grooming/boarding/vet), a tenant-favorable CAM (pro-rata + 5% admin, no capital/structural/management, with a soft 5% estimate cap), pro-rata taxes, free assignment for collateral/merger/metro-portfolio transfers (Landlord consent otherwise, not unreasonably withheld), and no continuous-operation covenant — though Landlord holds a go-dark recapture (180-day cessation) that requires Landlord to pay PetSmart a termination fee (up to $500K). PetSmart's own co-tenancy protection (a first-5-years King Soopers clause) has long since expired, so there is no ongoing co-tenancy. The full document folder was enumerated and read; the abstract reconciles cleanly with the April-2026 rent roll. One transition item is flagged: the 2011 DDR fixed-CAM agreement should have dropped off when KPR bought the center, reverting PetSmart to lease pro-rata CAM — worth confirming how it's being billed.
